ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 24-hour history of a new, left-sided throbbing headache.  
  • No clear precipitating trigger identified; patient notes recent work-related stress.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Onset on waking yesterday morning; pain intensity fluctuates but never fully resolves.  
  • Photophobia reported (worse in bright rooms/sunlight).  
  • Pain reportedly improves when lying down.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: No swelling/closure sensation, no voice change, no dysphagia/odynophagia, no drooling.  
  • Nose/eyes: Photophobia only; no nasal congestion or ocular watering/itching.  
  • Airway/breathing: No dyspnea, no stridor, no noisy breathing.  
  • Swelling: No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling.  
  • Ear/neck: No ear pain, hearing change, neck pain, or neck swelling.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Denies prior headaches or migraines.  
  • No previous ED visits or hospitalizations for similar complaints.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergic to Aspirin (causes severe nausea) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Current medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) and Microgynon combined oral contraceptive pill (daily).  
  • Occasional prior use of NSAIDs (Ibuprofen), none taken in past few days.

- Social context:
  • Lives with housemates; no mention of supervision required.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported or observed via teleconsultation.  
- Airway/breathing: Patient speaking in full sentences; no reported respiratory distress.  
- Mental status: Alert, coherent.  
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (telephone consultation).  
- Accompaniment: Patient alone during call.

Assessment:
- Likely first presentation of migraine-type headache (unilateral, throbbing, photophobia, improved with rest; no red-flag neurological or ENT features).  
- No clinical evidence of ENT infectious focus or allergic/anaphylactic process.

Plan:
- Analgesia: Continue Paracetamol; initiate NSAID (Ibuprofen) with food if tolerated, provided no previous adverse reaction other than aspirin-induced nausea was noted.  
- Hydration: Increase oral fluid intake.  
- Monitoring/Red flags: Seek urgent medical review if headache worsens, new neurological deficit develops, fever appears, rash emerges, or any ENT airway symptoms (voice change, throat swelling, breathing difficulty) occur.  
- Self-care tools: Obtain a thermometer for home monitoring.  
- Blood pressure: Arrange check at local pharmacy/GP within the next few days.  
- Follow-up: Re-contact clinic if pain not settling with above measures, if headaches become recurrent, or if menstrual-related pattern suspected for further evaluation.  
- Education: Discussed typical migraine features, potential stress link, and importance of identifying future triggers.

Quality checks
● Missing elements: No vital signs, no formal neurological or ENT examination, no detailed headache diary, no discussion of family migraine management strategies, no documentation of availability of NSAID-alternative analgesics given aspirin sensitivity.  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional conversational fillers but clinically adequate.
